headline: Broadcasters spent the week moving their catalogues into other companies' apps, and nobody said how a title gets found once it is one tile among thousands there.
summary: Channel 4 will put its channel and catalogue on Disney+ from early 2027 (27 Oct), TF1 credits Netflix for 20.5% TF1+ ad growth (29 Oct), and Versant built four more FAST channels from existing shows (28 Oct).

Microdrama money went into new vertical content: Fox and Endemol Shine's 30-episode Fear Factor (28 Oct), JLA Play licensing about 30 DramaBox series (27 Oct) and a Korean webtoon slate. None of the deals mines existing long-form.
Asking the TV for something by mood is becoming standard (Apple TV with Siri AI on sale 13 Nov), and no launch says where the mood data comes from.
Competitors were quiet: the only vendor item in the window was Veritone's Q3 call notice. The search index seems to lag about ten days, so read this as 'not surfaced'.

Zero new third-party mentions for the second week running. The TVBEurope Best of Show listing for the Agentic Layer now has two search quotes but still needs a first-hand check. Satis starts Wednesday.

ideas.hook: Channel 4 is moving its channel and catalogue into Disney+ next year, and I keep wondering how a Disney+ viewer will come across a Channel 4 drama they weren't looking for.
ideas.angle: Broadcasters are putting their catalogues inside apps they don't run: Channel 4 on Disney+ in the UK and Ireland from early 2027, and TF1 crediting its Netflix partnership for TF1+ growth. Inside someone else's interface the broadcaster no longer controls the home screen. What it still controls is how each title is described, the artwork that represents it and the preview that plays when someone pauses on it. Write this for the broadcasters in the DPP audience.
ideas.proof: Metadata Enrichment and Custom Thumbnails for broadcasters; the IVORY partnership for France and Benelux is public.

ideas.hook: If I ran a Nordic broadcaster, I would be reading TF1's third-quarter numbers very closely this week.
ideas.angle: TF1 reports TF1+ advertising up 20.5% in the third quarter and streaming consumption up 25%, and credits the Netflix partnership. A view from Stockholm on what SVT, NRK, Yle or TV4 could take from that: partner for reach, and keep tight hold of how the catalogue is described and shown wherever it appears. Check both figures on TF1's official release before posting.

ideas.hook: This week Fox ordered a 30-episode vertical Fear Factor and a new French streamer licensed about 30 vertical series. All of that money went into new content, while scenes that already work on a phone sit unused in film archives.
ideas.angle: Three deals in one week (Fox and Endemol Shine for My Drama, JLA Play and DramaBox, a Korean webtoon slate) all buy content made for vertical from the start. Long-form libraries already hold short, self-contained scenes that could feed a vertical feed; the work is choosing which ones. Same thesis as 2026-W44-06 with fresh news, so post one of the two.
ideas.proof: Preview Clips & Shorts, selecting moments by emotional arc.

ideas.hook: From 13 November you can ask the new Apple TV for a film by mood. Someone who signed up yesterday will ask too, and for them the only thing the system can go on is what's inside the films.
ideas.angle: Mood and plot requests are now a standard TV feature (Apple TV with Siri AI on sale 13 Nov, TiVo, Samsung, EE). For a viewer with a long history, behaviour fills the gaps. For a new viewer there is no history, so the answer depends entirely on metadata about the content. A 30-second screen recording of day-one mood rows makes the point better than words.
ideas.proof: Curio: mood rows for a viewer with two titles watched (the Curio landing-page visual).

ideas.hook: AI agents have started buying TV ads from other AI agents. From what I can see, neither side knows much about what happens inside the shows being bought.
ideas.angle: Fox is reported to have extended agent-based buying to linear and live TV with several agency groups, and CNN International is testing how language models read its inventory. Both stories are about how the deal gets done. An agent can only weigh what it can read, and today that is mostly show titles and genres. Check both articles' dates before posting.
ideas.proof: Scene and emotion metadata as structured input that buying agents can read.

ideas.hook: The US TV industry won't get its monthly Nielsen scoreboard for September and October until later this year. I doubt many streamers will notice in their product decisions, because the signals behind those decisions come from their own apps.
ideas.angle: Nielsen is publishing September and October together after a change in method (partly verified). The Gauge tells you share of viewing. It can't tell you which title a viewer scrolled past or which preview made them press play. Those answers come from first-party data joined to an understanding of the content itself.
ideas.proof: Viewer-outcome measurement around thumbnails, previews and Curio rows.

reactsTo.label: Nielsen The Gauge: September and October to be published together later this year

ideas.hook: Versant launched four FAST channels this week built entirely from shows that already exist. I would love to know how much of the episode picking and ad-break placement was done by hand.
ideas.angle: Turning a library into a channel means choosing episodes that sit well next to each other, placing breaks that don't cut through a scene, and making art that reads as a channel. Vionlabs automates most of that work for FAST and AVOD services. Ask the question with genuine curiosity rather than as a pitch.
ideas.proof: Ad-Break Creation and Custom Thumbnails; the FAST/AVOD ICP.

reactsTo.label: Versant launches new FAST channels from CNBC, Oxygen and E! shows (NewscastStudio)

ideas.hook: Choosing one frame to represent a two-hour film sounds like a small job. Here is how we approach it, including the frames we throw away.
ideas.angle: Thumbnails haven't come up in the radar's ideas yet. Show four or five candidate frames from one public-domain or licensed title, which ones the model rejected and why (closed eyes, motion blur, a spoiler, a mood that doesn't match the film), and the one it picked. HBO Max still has editors choose its Shorts moments, which shows how much judgement this takes.
ideas.proof: Custom Thumbnails; needs real examples from the product team. Don't invent numbers.

reactsTo.label: HBO Max embraces vertical video with a Shorts feed (TechCrunch)

ideas.hook: YouTube now takes 15.8% of all US TV viewing and is bringing Shorts to the living-room screen. As far as we can find, every streamer's clip feed still lives only on the phone.
ideas.angle: The August Gauge put YouTube at a record 15.8% of US TV time, and more than a third of YouTube's ad revenue now comes from TV screens. Streamers' vertical feeds are built for phones. The previews and clips that would compete on the TV itself have to be cut from the long-form catalogue, in landscape.
ideas.proof: Preview Clips & Shorts in both orientations.

reactsTo.label: Nielsen Gauge: YouTube record 15.8% of US TV time (Tubefilter)
